source.title: Arousal-Biased Competition in Perception and Memory.

confidence_rationale: Provides the mechanistic theory that arousal is a PRIORITY-WEIGHTED (not uniform) modulator -- it enhances high-priority representations and impairs low-priority ones -- which is precisely the vector-not-scalar constraint at the heart of MECH-074b. Confidence moderate because the theory operates primarily at perception/encoding and does not specifically assert a retrieval-time weight applied to stored hippocampal traces, and because it is a theoretical synthesis rather than a single decisive experiment.
failure_signatures: Arousal-biased competition sets priority largely at perception/encoding and via consolidation; the theory does not require, and does not by itself supply, a retrieval-time re-weighting of already-stored traces, so it under-determines MECH-074b's specific retrieval locus.

The theory predicts arousal will sometimes IMPAIR memory (for low-priority items); if REE's substrate applied the weight only additively (w_i = 1 + alpha*tag_i, always >= 1) it could reproduce relative enhancement of central items but not the absolute suppression of peripheral items that ABC and the lesion data both show.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Arousal during an event increases the bias in favour of high-priority stimuli in both perception and long-term memory; arousal-biased competition theory predicts when arousal will enhance memory for events and when it will impair it, resolving contradictions in the emotional-memory literature.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-074b's core design decision -- a per-trace weight vector rather than a scalar gain -- is the substrate realisation of arousal-biased competition: high-priority (central/threat-associated) traces get amplified weight, low-priority (peripheral) traces are relatively suppressed. ABC is the theoretical warrant that the biologically correct modulation is priority-weighted, so a scalar 'retrieval gain on all traces' is the wrong functional form.
mapping.mapping_caveat: ABC is agentic about WHEN priority is set (bottom-up salience + top-down goals, mostly at perception/encoding) but agnostic-to-contrary about MECH-074b's claim that the weight is applied at RETRIEVAL and grows with trace age. The theory also predicts genuine impairment of low-priority items, which a purely additive w_i >= 1 rule cannot produce -- a substrate-form caveat, not just a locus caveat.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical review / model synthesis across human perception and memory; integrates behavioural, neuroimaging and pharmacological findings.

confidence_components.notes: Influential, highly-cited theoretical synthesis (high citation impact, but a review not an experiment -> source_quality 0.75). Mapping fidelity high on the vector-not-scalar point, discounted by the retrieval-locus gap and the additive-vs-competitive form issue. Transfer risk moderate: human attention/memory theory -> REE hippocampal readout.
